sources.fact: The Spring 2026 update is a January 2026 snapshot and keeps fixed coverage, FWA, take-up, satellite and mobile evidence separate.
sources.guard: Do not convert area or snapshot coverage into a selected-address retail order.

sources.fact: Operator plans as at January 2026 cover deployment to the end of 2028 and include stated confidence categories.
sources.guard: Even a high-confidence plan is not evidence of current activation or orderability.

sources.fact: The checker presents operator-supplied predictions and requires the user to preserve the selected property context.
sources.guard: A predicted or partial-area result must not be copied to every address in the postcode.

sources.fact: The broadband USO is a request and eligibility assessment that considers existing service, planned public build and cost.
sources.guard: USO eligibility is not a live service, accepted order or completed installation.

sources.fact: The May 2026 NR OMR requests current and three-year planned gigabit coverage and runs in January, May and September.
sources.guard: Supplier submissions are planning evidence, not delivery or order commitments.

sources.fact: The June 2026 publication provides January OMR and BDUK-plan outputs with a UPRN-level technical note and sample.
sources.guard: Retain the release epoch and do not merge samples or outputs from different review rounds.

sources.fact: The collection separates current gigabit connectivity, future commercial plans and BDUK intervention plans at UPRN level.
sources.guard: Current, future and intervention fields must remain separate from retail orderability.

sources.fact: The RFI evaluates supplier claims at UPRN level and distinguishes White, Under Review and Grey voucher states.
sources.guard: A voucher project, issued voucher or claimed voucher has different evidence strength and must not be collapsed.

sources.fact: OS Places defines Find, Postcode and UPRN capture requests separately from Nearest, BBOX, Radius and Polygon searches.
sources.guard: Spatial candidates are not exact address or UPRN matches.

sources.fact: The UPRN endpoint requires a valid identifier and returns dataset, epoch, last-update, match and CRS metadata.
sources.guard: Retain header metadata and lifecycle dataset before binding service evidence.

sources.fact: DPA and LPI are distinct address datasets and not every property has an associated DPA record.
sources.guard: DPA absence is not proof that the property or UPRN is absent.

sources.fact: Live projects permit 600 transactions per minute per API and project; development projects permit 50.
sources.guard: A 429 response is a temporary technical state and must never be stored as NO_DATA.

sources.fact: The OpenData API links property, street and OS MasterMap identifiers across datasets.
sources.guard: Identifier correlation is not ownership, legal boundary or broadband evidence.

sources.fact: The API exposes identifier, identifier-type, feature-type and product-version endpoints.
sources.guard: Store product version and relationship method before accepting a link.

sources.fact: The checker requires postcode then address selection and distinguishes order-now, soon, planned, building and no-plan states.
sources.guard: Only the selected address and current order-now state can support orderability.

sources.fact: Openreach maintains the network while a broadband provider places the order and arranges activation.
sources.guard: A network result is not an accepted retail order or installed service.

sources.fact: Visible construction can precede testing, activation and broadband-provider onboarding; package options may vary by provider.
sources.guard: Street build and network reach do not prove property-level retail availability.

sources.fact: Interest registration is free and non-binding; property-owner permission or a wayleave may still be required.
sources.guard: Interest, demand and permission workflows are not order acceptance or installation.

sources.fact: The May OMR closed on 1 June 2026; submissions entered evaluation and postcode/UPRN outputs were pending publication.
sources.guard: Closure or submission receipt is not assessed coverage; hold until the evaluated output is published.

sources.fact: Supplier-name errors were identified and the September 2025 files were replaced on 2 February 2026.
sources.guard: Superseded files and supplier labels must not survive a corrected release.

sources.fact: BDUK plans updated releases alongside OMR publications about every four months and describes correction of UPRN/address errors.
sources.guard: Retain release date; treat reported data errors as correction workflows, not property absence.

sources.fact: OS Places uses AddressBase Premium, updates daily and supports address, postcode, UPRN and spatial search but not unrestricted bulk querying.
sources.guard: Do not infer national completeness from throttled interactive API attempts.

sources.fact: An identifier query may return more than one link set because UPRN and USRN numeric namespaces can overlap.
sources.guard: Use identifier type or feature type; do not accept a numeric ID without namespace disambiguation.

sources.fact: Feature-type queries explicitly support BLPU, road and topographic feature classes and document 400/401/403/404/429/500/503 responses.
sources.guard: Wrong feature type and technical HTTP states are not valid empty property results.

sources.fact: Wrong or missing results can arise from address formatting or network-record matching and can be investigated.
sources.guard: A mismatch remains unresolved until corrected; do not store it as NO_DATA.

sources.fact: Adjacent premises can differ because of network design, building type, landlord permission or timing.
sources.guard: Never transfer a neighbour's availability or orderability to the target address.

sources.fact: Private-road status is a checker dependency that can affect access and build assumptions.
sources.guard: Road classification or permission uncertainty is not proof of service unavailability or property absence.

sources.fact: Address information is reviewed and updated and a missing or incorrect checker entry can persist temporarily.
sources.guard: Hold the address for correction and recheck; do not infer permanent NO_DATA.

sources.fact: The checker requires postcode entry followed by address selection and returns packages available for that address.
sources.guard: Postcode entry, selected address and package eligibility must remain separate.

sources.fact: Users outside the current footprint can register for notifications about future expansion.
sources.guard: A notification or interest registration is not a build commitment, order or installation.

sources.fact: The retail journey separates availability checking, package choice, installation-date selection and engineer connection.
sources.guard: Availability and package selection do not prove installation completion.

sources.fact: Location pages describe survey and road/pavement preparation as stages before network build and service readiness.
sources.guard: Survey or visible build activity is not address-level orderability.

sources.fact: Residential service requires the home to be within the live network and instructs users to check their postcode.
sources.guard: Borough or street marketing must not substitute for the selected-home checker result.

sources.fact: YouFibre presents address eligibility and packages through a postcode flow that can also return a server-error state.
sources.guard: A server error is a technical failure, not a negative availability result.

sources.fact: Quarterly coverage distinguishes existing footprint and build locations and warns that not every premise in a listed location has service.
sources.guard: Location-level ready-for-service totals cannot be copied to every property.

sources.fact: nexfibre is a wholesale network and directs consumers to an ISP partner's postcode checker for retail services.
sources.guard: Wholesale footprint, ISP onboarding and selected-address retail availability must remain separate.
